exposure: Special Supplemental Nutritional Program for Women, Infants, and Children enrollment
outcome: Introduction of other liquids within 1 week postpartum
cohort: 42,778 primiparous women with low income and singleton gestations who gave birth at term and responded to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System between 2009 and 2018
finding: This study found that while WIC enrollment was not significantly associated with exclusive breastfeeding rates after 1 week postpartum, women enrolled in WIC were less likely to ever breastfeed and more likely to introduce formula within the first week.
mod_finding: While there was no significant difference in exclusive breastfeeding rates based on WIC enrollment, the study found that women enrolled in WIC were less likely to ever breastfeed and more likely to introduce formula within the first week postpartum.
